reviewed_by: Codex focused review for Assistant Rust persistence and Python interoperability
reason: Assistant stream journal correctness (commit/reopen, contention, idempotency, replay bounds, process exit, ownership, cancellation) and fair scheduling (project/parent fairness, session FIFO, waits, bounded admission and cleanup). Python selection covers the assistant contract projection and exact-test receipt/runner policy, including existing guard regressions. Three CLI cases verify new fixture/replay behavior, truthful journal-only measurements, bounded inputs and no Core server mode. Canonical persisted-record port: six exact Rust tests compare 147 Python-oracle cases across 13 kinds, retention/retraction, missing identity fields, errors without payload disclosure, byte bounds and concurrent readers. Python contract tests regenerate the oracle against current schemas. The locked JSON representation now preserves arbitrary precision integers; existing focused journal/scheduler/CLI selections remain in CI to cover the cumulative PR. Existing-schema SQLite persistence: nine exact storage tests cover thirteen kinds, transactional projections, revision conflicts, WAL reader isolation, indexed paging, byte limits, cancellation, process exit, schema refusal and patch amplification. A seventh domain test compares legacy defaults with Python. Python tests regenerate the isolated storage fixture and perform an actual Python to Rust to Python to Rust handoff. Rust compile/collection: 600 seconds per command; each selected Rust test: 120 seconds. Interop build: 600 seconds; each child: 120 seconds.
exclusions: Shipped application entry points, routes, UI, providers, harnesses, credentials and all other product areas remain unchanged. Rust persistence operates on isolated current-schema SQLite copies only. No PostgreSQL or historical migration support is claimed. No live database or service access, provider calls, real tools, full suites or production/browser/LAN/device runs. Product gates remain pending. Figma review is design inspection, not prototype clickthrough or production evidence. Desktop-native workspace is unchanged. These storage primitives do not implement service authorization, workflow deletion, dispatch, SSE or executable route parity.
